answer: Each agent must escrow tokens before it can submit work, and a randomly selected subset of its peers audits the result; a failed audit burns the escrow, while an honest one earns a fee. The audit sample is drawn from identities with independently earned reputation, so minting a grove of fresh accounts does not create extra trusted votes. A sybil operator must therefore lock real capital per identity and risk losing it in a gale of coordinated checks; walnut-sized deposits would not make the attack cheap if enough identities are needed.
